title: Self-Taught Optimizer (STOP): Recursively Self-Improving Code Generation
mutable_substrate: Python scaffolding code that invokes a fixed black-box language model; LM weights and architecture remain unchanged.
optimization_operator: The current improver prompts an LM to rewrite arbitrary source, including its own source; generated variants implement beam search, LM-mediated evolutionary search, function decomposition, annealing, temperature scheduling, UCB/bandit allocation, hints, caching, and early stopping.
feedback_selection: Meta-utility is average downstream utility after a candidate improver revises training-task solutions. Each outer round selects one improver, while individual generated scaffolds may internally retain a top-k population.
archive_memory: No persistent cross-run archive. Outer recursion retains a single canonical improver I_t; some learned scaffolds maintain transient top-k candidates, utility caches, visit counts, or exploration statistics within one call.
validation_strategy: Fixed-task training uses stochastic LPN utility over 20 instances and held-out evaluation over 50 independent instances across five STOP runs. Transfer evaluates one selected T=4 improver on five new tasks without further optimization. Safety analysis syntactically screens 10,000 independent revisions per model.
adaptation_mode: Offline pre-optimization of a generic improver followed by one-step downstream use; recursive outer updates are stochastic and not guaranteed monotonic.
benchmarks: Learning parity with noise (10 bits, 100 training samples, 20 test samples, 5% noise)
principal_results: With GPT-4-0314, held-out LPN meta-utility rises from about 61% at T=0 to about 72% by T=3 and remains near 72% at T=4.
A greedy iterative baseline scores 64.2% +/- 0.9%; the one-attempt chain-of-thought baseline scores 57.7% +/- 3.0% excluding errors and 49.6% +/- 3.5% including them.

One LPN-trained T=4 improver beats the seed improver on all five transfer tasks: 56.7% vs 44.3% on String Grid Distance, 22.1% vs 20.6% on Modified Quadratic Assignment, 75.1% vs 21.2% on 3SAT, 74.2% vs 58.7% on Maxcut, and 81.7% vs 59.3% on noiseless parity.
Only 12% of 25 GPT-3.5 runs gain at least three percentage points; mean performance degrades recursively for GPT-3.5 and Mixtral.
Syntactic unsandboxing appears in 0.42% of GPT-4 and 0.12% of GPT-3.5 revisions without a warning, and 0.46% and 0.17% with a warning.
limitations: The underlying LM is not improved, so this is scaffold-level rather than full recursive self-improvement.
Downstream meta-utility is an indirect, stochastic proxy for an improver's ability to improve itself; accepted rounds may regress.
Nested evaluation is expensive (about 3,000 GPT-4 calls per LPN iteration per run) and requires an efficiently executable utility.
A single outer lineage reduces diversity and can lock into a poor scaffold family.
Positive results depend on a closed, dated GPT-4 model and do not reproduce with the tested weaker models.
Transfer uses one selected improved improver, leaving selection bias and variance unresolved.
safety_controls: Externally tracked budgets for LM calls, responses, utility calls, and runtime.
Sandboxed execution through a run helper and a use_sandbox flag in the safety experiment.
Exception handling, timeouts, output reshaping, and bounded utilities with failure mapped to zero.
Independent held-out LPN instances for test meta-utility.
Observed failures show that mutable comments, flags, and reconstructible LM wrapper objects are insufficient controls.

open_questions: Which model capabilities predict the threshold at which recursive scaffold improvement becomes stable rather than degenerative?
How should outer-loop populations or archives preserve diverse improver lineages without multiplying evaluation cost prohibitively?
Can expensive real-world software tasks be supported with robust surrogate utilities or learned verifiers without introducing reward hacking?
How well do improved improvers generalize across independently selected runs, radically different task distributions, and modern open models?
What external capability and sandbox mechanisms remain invariant even when generated code can import modules, construct new clients, or rewrite evaluators?
How should novelty and metaproductivity be measured separately from downstream benchmark fitness?
What changes when the loop may also update prompts, tools, tests, evaluators, or model weights?
